item.title: The use of calcium
item.content:encoded:
Hi folks. Love this entry. What a primal horror concept. I do have one suggested edit.
It's the use of calcium. As a pure metal it is too reactive to exist in an oxygen atmosphere i.e. It would react rapidly with oxygen in air, ignite and explode violently.
I appreciate the use of dual air locks could help mitigate any reaction with calcium metal, but only if stated that the secondary containment chamber was kept under vacuum at all times. Even then, in the event of a containment breach oxygen would reach the calcium chamber and cause a reaction that could be violent enough to cause further breaches.
I'd suggest using another metal or a calcium compound that is non oxidising.
Excerpt from wikipedia - Hydroxylapatite (Ca5(PO4)3(OH)), but is usually written Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2) makes up seventy percent of bone. Carbonated-calcium deficient hydroxylapatite is the main mineral of which dental enamel and dentin are comprised.

For this article, I'd like to propose a link SCP-1219, which refers to an entity that appears only in dark spaces and that will disipate whenever it is exposed to light, which is something that we also see in this article. That being said, recommending the addition of the following footnote (code is intentionally broken):

Editing this:

SCP-575 appears to be an unknown form of matter, taking the form of a series of amorphous black shapes and structures. SCP-575 is difficult to observe, as it immediately dissipates when exposed to light.

To read:

SCP-575 appears to be an unknown form of matter, taking the form of a series of amorphous black shapes and structures. SCP-575 is difficult to observe, as it immediately dissipates when exposed to light[[footnote]]An action reminiscent of SCP-1219, however a connection between the two entities has not yet been made[/footnote]].

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Keep in mind that heat is emitted in infrared photons, and radio waves go more or less everywhere. "Total darkness" may be possible in terms of visible light, but there is always some form of light, be it infrared, radio, or whatever.

But yeah, that should be edited to reflect that. Perhaps "complete or nearly complete absence of visible light"?
